speaker: Doctor
text: That's a bit unusual; could you please describe the appearance of the skin lesions and tell me if they are itchy or painful? Also, when did you first notice the fever and wrist pain, and did you have any recent insect bites or travel to a forested area?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do the skin lesions have a central punctum or an "bull's-eye" appearance, and were they present before or after your knee pain? Also, have you noticed any rash on your palms or soles, and did you see any ticks while camping?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Early-stage Lyme Arthritis (Erythema Chronicum Migrans and Acral Pustular Rash) with concurrent reactive arthritis or septic arthritis.

Please have the patient immediately undergo joint aspiration of the left wrist to rule out septic arthritis and request a two-tiered Lyme serology (ELISA followed by Western Blot).
